**Given:** The setting, family and preparation (P) of the Statement: charge $q\in\mathbb R$ and mass $m>0$ ([[def-em-sources]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]); the plane-wave data $\kappa,e,\omega$ with $|\kappa|=\omega/c$, $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $b=\kappa\times e/\omega$; the family $r_\eta$ on the common open interval $I\ni0$ with the uniform first-order expansion about $x_0$; the first-order function $r_1\in C^2(I;\mathbb R^3)$; the harmonic data $w=(q/m)e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}$ and $z_p(t)=\operatorname{Re}(-w\omega^{-2}e^{-i\omega t})$.

[F1] Adopted force law (external supplier, whose carrier is the referenced in-run item): under its postulates, with the coordinate reading $r$, velocity $v=r'$ and $\gamma=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ of a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline in a prescribed exterior field $(E,B)$, the coordinate momentum $p=m\gamma v$ satisfies $\frac{dp}{dt}=q(E+v\times B)$ and $\frac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}=qE\cdot v$; the norm $\eta(U,U)$ is constant and a solution with future timelike data remains future timelike; and for every $\delta\in(0,1)$, wherever $|v|/c\le\delta$, $|\gamma-1|\le\frac{|v|^2/c^2}{2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}}$ and $|p-mv|\le m|v|\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}}$, with constants depending only on $\delta$; the statement is conditional on the adopted postulates and excludes self-force, radiation reaction and material media ([[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]], [[def-em-sources]], [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]]).

[F2] Plane-wave fields: $E_{\rm inc}(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(e\,e^{i(\kappa\cdot x-\omega t)})$, $B_{\rm inc}=\kappa\times E_{\rm inc}/\omega$ are jointly $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ ([[def-em-plane-wave-definition]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]); in particular, on every compact subset of $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ they are bounded and uniformly continuous with bounded first derivatives, and on a compact interval $L\subset I$ the maps $t\mapsto E_{\rm inc}(x_0,t)$, $t\mapsto B_{\rm inc}(x_0,t)$ are continuous ([[thm-extreme-value-metric]], [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]).

[F3] Harmonic response lemma: for $\omega>0$, $T=2\pi/\omega$, $w\in\mathbb C^3$, the particular solution $z_p(t)=\operatorname{Re}(-w\omega^{-2}e^{-i\omega t})$ is $C^\infty$ with $z_p''=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ and is $T$-periodic; every $C^2$ solution of that equation on $\mathbb R$ is $z_p+a+bt$ with unique $a,b$; it is $T$-periodic if and only if $b=0$; on any nonempty open interval the local solutions have a unique global extension $Z$; with $b=z'(t_*)-z_p'(t_*)$, and for $b=0$ the mean over every complete period is $a$ ([[lem-em-harmonic-forcing-periodic-response]]).

[F4] Cross-section theorem: for the ideal harmonic model with incident amplitude $e$ and dipole amplitude $p_0$, the total model cross section is $\sigma=\frac{\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4|e|^2}=\frac{\mu_0^2\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi|e|^2}$, and the scalar branch with $p_0=\alpha e$ is $\frac{\omega^4|\alpha|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4}$; the result assumes Countable Choice as carried by its suppliers ([[pthm-em-dipole-scattering-cross-section]], [[def-countable-choice]]).

[F5] Elementary calculus and algebra: vector-valued differentiation and integration are componentwise ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]); the second fundamental theorem evaluates $\int_a^bG'=G(b)-G(a)$ for integrable $G'$ ([[thm-ftc-second-part]]), a continuous real function on a closed interval is Riemann integrable ([[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]), the first fundamental theorem differentiates the integral function ([[thm-ftc-first-part]]), and $m\le f\le M$ on $[a,b]$ gives $m(b-a)\le\int_a^bf\le M(b-a)$ with the corresponding error bound ([[lem-integral-elementary-bounds]]); sums, products and compositions of differentiable maps obey the algebra and chain rules ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]); the cross product is bilinear and alternating with $|u\times v|\le|u||v|$ ([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]); and $|e^{i\theta}|=1$ for real $\theta$ ([[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]).

1.1 [Uniform smallness of the velocity and of $\gamma-1$] Let $K\subset I$ be a nonempty compact interval containing $0$ in its interior (any compact subinterval of $I$ containing $0$ will do); the expansion hypothesis gives $|v_\eta(t)|\le|\eta||\dot r_1(t)|+C_K\eta^2\le|\eta|(\|\dot r_1\|_K+C_K)$ for $|\eta|<\eta_0$ and $t\in K$, where $\|\dot r_1\|_K$ is finite by continuity on the compact $K$. Choose $\eta_1\in(0,\min\{\eta_0,1\})$ with $\eta_1(\|\dot r_1\|_K+C_K)\le c/2$; then for $0<|\eta|<\eta_1$ every $t\in K$ has $|v_\eta(t)|/c\le1/2$, so the low-speed clause of [F1] with $\delta=1/2$ gives $|\gamma_\eta(t)-1|\le\frac{|v_\eta(t)|^2}{2c^2(1-1/4)^{3/2}}\le C_1\eta^2$ for a constant $C_1$ depending only on $K,\eta_1$ and the data, uniformly in $t\in K$. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 [Uniform convergence of the scaled momentum and of its derivative] With $\gamma_\eta=(1-|v_\eta|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ and $P_\eta:=m\gamma_\eta v_\eta$, write $\frac1\eta P_\eta=m\gamma_\eta\frac{v_\eta}\eta=m\frac{v_\eta}\eta+m(\gamma_\eta-1)\frac{v_\eta}\eta$; by the expansion hypothesis $\frac{v_\eta}\eta\to\dot r_1$ uniformly on $K$ with error $C_K|\eta|$, and by step 1.1 $|\gamma_\eta-1|\le C_1\eta^2$ while $\bigl|\frac{v_\eta}\eta\bigr|\le\|\dot r_1\|_K+C_K|\eta|$ is uniformly bounded, so $\frac{P_\eta}\eta\to m\dot r_1$ uniformly on $K$ as $\eta\to0$ with $\eta\ne0$. Moreover, dividing the exact coordinate force law of [F1] by $\eta$ gives, for $t\in K$ and $\eta\ne0$, $\frac1\eta P_\eta'(t)=q\bigl[E_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(t),t)+v_\eta(t)\times B_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(t),t)\bigr]$, and this right-hand side converges uniformly on $K$ to $qE_{\rm inc}(x_0,t)$: the fields are uniformly continuous on a compact tube around $\{x_0\}\times K$ and $r_\eta(t)\to x_0$ uniformly by the expansion, while $|v_\eta(t)\times B_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(t),t)|\le|v_\eta(t)|\sup|B_{\rm inc}|\le C_2|\eta|$ by [F2] and the bilinearity and norm bound of [F5]. [step 1.1, given, F1, F2, F5, algebra]

3.1 [First-order equation] Fix $\eta\ne0$ with $|\eta|<\eta_1$ and fix a component index $i$. The scalar map $t\mapsto(P_\eta)_i(t)$ is $C^1$ on $K$ with continuous derivative $(P_\eta')_i=q\eta[E_{\rm inc}+v_\eta\times B_{\rm inc}]_i$, so $(P_\eta')_i$ is Riemann integrable on every closed subinterval of $K$ by [F5]; splitting at $0$ and applying the second fundamental theorem [F5] to the intervals $[0,t]$ for $t\ge0$ and $[t,0]$ for $t\le0$ (with the orientation convention of the displayed one-sided differences) gives, for every $t\in K$, $\frac{(P_\eta)_i(t)-(P_\eta)_i(0)}\eta=\int_0^t\frac{(P_\eta')_i(s)}\eta\,ds=q\int_0^t[E_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(s),s)+v_\eta(s)\times B_{\rm inc}(r_\eta(s),s)]_i\,ds$. By the uniform convergence of step 2.1 applied componentwise, the integrands converge uniformly on $K$ to $qE_{\rm inc}(x_0,\cdot)_i$, so the integral bound of [F5] lets $\eta\to0$: the left side tends to $m[(\dot r_1)_i(t)-(\dot r_1)_i(0)]$ and the right side to $q\int_0^tE_{\rm inc}(x_0,s)_i\,ds$. The fundamental theorem [F5] differentiates the right side in $t$ to $qE_{\rm inc}(x_0,t)_i$, and the left side is differentiable with derivative $m(\ddot r_1)_i(t)$; hence $m\ddot r_1(t)=qE_{\rm inc}(x_0,t)$ componentwise on $K$. Every point $t\in I$ lies in such a compact $K\subset I$ containing $0$, so the identity holds on all of $I$ and is clause (a). [step 2.1, F2, F5, algebra]

5.1 [Thomson cross section] Apply the cross-section formula of [F4] with the incident amplitude $e$ and dipole amplitude $p_0$ of step 4.1: $\sigma=\frac{\omega^4|p_0|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2c^4|e|^2}$, and $|p_0|^2=\frac{q^4}{m^2\omega^4}|e|^2$ because $|e^{i\kappa\cdot x_0}|=1$; substituting cancels $\omega^4$ and $|e|^2$ and gives $\sigma_{\rm T}=\frac{q^4}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2m^2c^4}$. Multiplying out, $\frac{8\pi}{3}\bigl(\frac{q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0mc^2}\bigr)^2=\frac{8\pi}{3}\cdot\frac{q^4}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0^2m^2c^4}=\frac{q^4}{6\pi\varepsilon_0^2m^2c^4}$, the same value, and it depends neither on $\omega$ nor on the phase factor beyond the unimodular $e'$; this is clause (c). [step 4.1, F4, F5, algebra]

(iv) **Relation to the ring rest-synchronization holonomy.** On the fixed-height timelike cylinder $C = \{r = R,\ x^3 = x^3_0\}$, material worldlines have constant rotating label. Its rest lines instead vary $\varphi$ on an angular lift and satisfy $dt/d\varphi = \Omega R^2/(c^2 - \Omega^2R^2)$, being integral curves of $\partial_\varphi + [\Omega R^2/(c^2 - \Omega^2R^2)]\,\partial_t$; for $\Omega = 0$ they are $t = \text{constant}$ circles; one circuit $\varphi \to \varphi + 2 \pi$ has the chart-time holonomy $\Delta t_h = 2 \pi \Omega R^2/(c^2 - \Omega^2R^2) = (t_1 - t_2)/2$ and the receiver proper-time holonomy $\Delta \tau_h = \Delta t_h/\gamma = 2 \pi \Omega R^2/(c^2 \sqrt{1 - \Omega^2R^2/c^2}) = (1/2)(t_1 - t_2)/\gamma$, exactly half of the detector proper-time difference of (iii); for $\Omega = 0$ both holonomies vanish. The ambient three-dimensional rest distribution of the rotating congruence is nowhere integrable for $\Omega \neq 0$, so no ambient rest-simultaneity hypersurface exists, while the one-dimensional rest distribution restricted to the fixed-height cylinder $C$ is locally integrable and has the global holonomy just computed, nonvanishing exactly when $\Omega \neq 0$; the return-time computation of (iii) uses only the guided null curves and the material worldline and does not use either integrability property ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (c), [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]]).

Let $x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ be the chart of an inertial frame ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). Fix $R > 0$, a real $\Omega$ with $|\Omega| R < c$, a real $x^3_0$ and a real $\phi_0$, and put $\gamma := (1 - \Omega^2 R^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. A rigidly rotating circular ring of radius $R$ and height $x^3_0$ about the $x^3$-axis, with angular velocity $\Omega$, has material worldlines
(i) **The ring worldline and the ring congruence.** $W_{\phi_0}$ is a $C^\infty$ future timelike worldline with unit observer

$\eta(n,n) = -1$, and four-velocity $U = c n = \gamma\,\partial_t|_{\varphi}$, $\eta(U,U) = -c^2$, where $\varphi := \phi - \Omega t$ is the rotating angular label of the ring material points; it is an unparametrized flow line of the rigid-rotation congruence $n = \gamma(r)\,[\partial_0 + (\Omega/c)(-x^2\partial_1 + x^1\partial_2)]$ restricted to $r = R$, and its proper time $\tau$ and the chart time $t$ satisfy $d\tau = dt/\gamma$, so $\tau = t/\gamma + \tau_0$ for an arbitrary proper-time origin $\tau_0$ on this worldline ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (c), [[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]).

(iii) **Return times and differences.** The displayed guided curves have all-real mathematical extensions; emitted signals are their restrictions $t \ge 0$. On those extensions $C_+$ meets the worldline $W_{\phi_0}$ exactly at the chart times $2 \pi k R/(c - \Omega R)$, $k \in \mathbb Z$, and $C_-$ exactly at the chart times $2 \pi k R/(c + \Omega R)$, $k \in \mathbb Z$; the smallest positive meeting times are $t_1 := 2 \pi R/(c - \Omega R) > 0$ and $t_2 := 2 \pi R/(c + \Omega R) > 0$. Hence the two counter-propagating signals emitted at the same event reunite with the emitting material point at the reception events $W_{\phi_0}(t_1)$ and $W_{\phi_0}(t_2)$, each having gained exactly one circuit relative to that material point, and the chart-time difference of the two reunions is $t_1 - t_2 = 4 \pi \Omega R^2/(c^2 - \Omega^2 R^2) > 0$ for $\Omega > 0$. The proper-time difference measured by the detector ideal clock is $(t_1 - t_2)/\gamma = 4 \pi \Omega R^2/(c^2 \sqrt{1 - \Omega^2R^2/c^2})$. For $\Omega = 0$ (inertial ring) $t_1 = t_2 = 2 \pi R/c$ and both differences vanish; for $\Omega < 0$ the sign of the first difference reverses and the roles of $C_+$ and $C_-$ are interchanged.

(iv) **Relation to the ring rest-synchronization holonomy.** On the fixed-height timelike cylinder $C = \{r = R,\ x^3 = x^3_0\}$, material worldlines have constant rotating label. Its rest lines instead vary $\varphi$ on an angular lift and satisfy $dt/d\varphi = \Omega R^2/(c^2 - \Omega^2R^2)$, being integral curves of $\partial_\varphi + [\Omega R^2/(c^2 - \Omega^2R^2)]\,\partial_t$; for $\Omega = 0$ they are $t = \text{constant}$ circles; one circuit $\varphi \to \varphi + 2 \pi$ has the chart-time holonomy $\Delta t_h = 2 \pi \Omega R^2/(c^2 - \Omega^2R^2) = (t_1 - t_2)/2$ and the receiver proper-time holonomy $\Delta \tau_h = \Delta t_h/\gamma = 2 \pi \Omega R^2/(c^2 \sqrt{1 - \Omega^2R^2/c^2}) = (1/2)(t_1 - t_2)/\gamma$, exactly half of the detector proper-time difference of (iii); for $\Omega = 0$ both holonomies vanish. The ambient three-dimensional rest distribution of the rotating congruence is nowhere integrable for $\Omega \neq 0$, so no ambient rest-simultaneity hypersurface exists, while the one-dimensional rest distribution restricted to the fixed-height cylinder $C$ is locally integrable and has the global holonomy just computed, nonvanishing exactly when $\Omega \neq 0$; the return-time computation of (iii) uses only the guided null curves and the material worldline and does not use either integrability property ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (c), [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]]).

[L4] A curve $x:I\to A$ is differentiable precisely when its coordinate representation is, its tangent is the corresponding $V$-vector, and it is $C^k$ when that representation is; at a regular point the causal character and future direction of the curve are those of its tangent ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] (a),(b)).

[L5] Causal classification: timelike means $\eta(v,v)<0$, null means $v\neq0$ and $\eta(v,v)=0$, and each nonzero causal vector is future or past but not both; $C^+=\{v:v^0>|v_s|\}$ and $\bar C^+=\{v:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$ in every inertial chart ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], [[lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion]] (a)).

[L8] Derivatives: $(\sin t)'=\cos t$, $(\cos t)'=-\sin t$, and the chain rule differentiates composites with affine inner maps ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule]], [[def-derivative]]).

[L10] Rigid rotation and the ring: on the timelike region $r^2<c^2/\Omega^2$ the field $n=\gamma(r)[\partial_0+(\Omega/c)(-x^2\partial_1+x^1\partial_2)]$ is a smooth future unit timelike Born-rigid congruence with nowhere-zero vorticity for $\Omega\neq0$; on the ring cylinder $r=R$, $x^3=\text{const}$, the induced metric is $-(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)dt^2+2\Omega R^2\,dt\,d\varphi+R^2d\varphi^2$, the ring observer $\phi=\phi_0+\Omega t$ has $n=\gamma(R)(1,-(\Omega R/c)\sin\phi,(\Omega R/c)\cos\phi,0)$, the one-dimensional rest distribution is locally integrable with $dt/d\varphi=\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$, one positive circuit has signed chart-time offset $\Delta t=2\pi\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$, and for $\Omega=0$ the ring is inertial with rest lines $t=\text{const}$ ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (c)).

1.1 (Tangent and invariants of the ring worldline.) With $\varphi:=\phi_0+\Omega t$, the coordinate functions of $W_{\phi_0}$ are $t\mapsto ct$, $t\mapsto R\cos\varphi$, $t\mapsto R\sin\varphi$ and the constant $x^3_0$; differentiating with [L8] gives $\dot W=(c,-\Omega R\sin\varphi,\Omega R\cos\varphi,0)$, and by [L2] and [L9], $\eta(\dot W,\dot W)=-c^2+\Omega^2R^2(\sin^2\varphi+\cos^2\varphi)=-c^2(1-\Omega^2R^2/c^2)=-c^2/\gamma^2<0$, while the time component is $\dot W^0=c>0$ and the spatial part has Euclidean norm $|\Omega| R<c$. [L2, L3, L8, L9, algebra]

1.2 (The guided curves are future null.) With $\varphi_\pm:=\phi_0\pm ct/R$ the curves $C_\pm$ have coordinate functions $t\mapsto ct$, $t\mapsto R\cos\varphi_\pm$, $t\mapsto R\sin\varphi_\pm$; differentiating gives tangents $(c,\mp c\sin\varphi_\pm,\pm c\cos\varphi_\pm,0)$, whose $\eta$-square is $-c^2+c^2(\sin^2+\cos^2)=0$ by [L2] and [L9], so the tangent is nonzero null, with time component $c$ equal to the Euclidean norm of its spatial part; hence each tangent lies in $\bar C^+\setminus\{0\}$ by [L5], so each of $C_\pm$ is a future null curve. [L5, L8, L9, algebra]

1.3 (Rest-synchronization data on the cylinder.) By [L10] the induced metric on the cylinder is $-(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)dt^2+2\Omega R^2dt\,d\varphi+R^2d\varphi^2$ with $c^2-\Omega^2R^2>0$ by $|\Omega|R<c$, and the one-dimensional rest distribution is locally integrable with $dt/d\varphi=\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$; one positive circuit $\varphi\mapsto\varphi+2\pi$ has chart-time offset $\Delta t_h=2\pi\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$, and for $\Omega=0$ the rest lines are $t=\text{const}$. For $\Omega\neq0$ the ambient rest distribution has nowhere-zero vorticity, so by [L11] it is nowhere integrable and admits no local rest-simultaneity hypersurface; the rank-one cylinder distribution is a separate locally integrable object, and no global single-valued rest time on the cylinder exists when $\Delta t_h\neq0$. 2.1 (Congruence data and proper time on the ring.) By [L10] the field $n=\gamma(R)(1,-(\Omega R/c)\sin\varphi,(\Omega R/c)\cos\varphi,0)$ is the unit observer of the ring material point and $W_{\phi_0}$ is its flow line; direct substitution with [L9] gives $\eta(n,n)=\gamma^2(-1+(\Omega^2R^2/c^2)(\sin^2+\cos^2))=\gamma^2(-1+\Omega^2R^2/c^2)=-1$, and $U:=cn=c\gamma(1,-(\Omega R/c)\sin\varphi,(\Omega R/c)\cos\varphi,0)=\gamma\dot W$, coinciding with $\gamma\,\partial_t|_{\varphi}$ evaluated along the material line and with the four-velocity of [L6]. Since $\eta(\dot W,\dot W)=-c^2/\gamma^2$ by step 1.1, the proper-time integrand of [L7] is $c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta(\dot W,\dot W)}=1/\gamma$, so $d\tau=dt/\gamma$ and $\tau=t/\gamma+\tau_0$. 3.1 (The ring worldline is a future timelike worldline and a congruence flow line.) By step 1.1 the coordinate functions are smooth compositions of affine maps with sine and cosine, so $W_{\phi_0}$ is $C^\infty$ by [L4]; its tangent is timelike with positive time component exceeding the spatial norm, so it is future timelike and regular by [L5], and $W_{\phi_0}$ is a future timelike worldline. By step 2.1 it is a flow line of the unit field $n$ of the rigid-rotation congruence restricted to $r=R$, with four-velocity $U=cn$ and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ in agreement with [L6], and its proper time is $\tau=t/\gamma+\tau_0$ by step 2.1. [L4, L5, L6, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 (Return times and the differences.) Since $|\Omega|R<c$, both $c-\Omega R>0$ and $c+\Omega R>0$; hence the smallest positive members of the two meeting sets of step 2.2 are $t_1=2\pi R/(c-\Omega R)$ and $t_2=2\pi R/(c+\Omega R)$, both positive, and the emitted signals reunite with the emitting material point at $W_{\phi_0}(t_1)$ and $W_{\phi_0}(t_2)$ after exactly one circuit relative to it. Their chart-time difference is $t_1-t_2=2\pi R\bigl[(c+\Omega R)-(c-\Omega R)\bigr]/((c-\Omega R)(c+\Omega R))=4\pi\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$, which is positive for $\Omega>0$ and negative for $\Omega<0$. By step 3.1 the two receptions correspond to proper times $\tau=t_1/\gamma+\tau_0$ and $\tau=t_2/\gamma+\tau_0$ of the detector ideal clock, so the detector reads the proper-time difference $(t_1-t_2)/\gamma=4\pi\Omega R^2/(c^2\sqrt{1-\Omega^2R^2/c^2})$ by [L1] and step 2.1. [L1, L2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 2.2, algebra]

5.1 (Holonomy and the factor-two relation.) By step 1.3 the chart-time holonomy of the ring rest lines over one circuit is $\Delta t_h=2\pi\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$; comparing with step 4.1 gives $t_1-t_2=2\Delta t_h$, i.e. $\Delta t_h=(t_1-t_2)/2$. Dividing by $\gamma$ using $d\tau=dt/\gamma$ of step 2.1 gives the receiver proper-time holonomy $\Delta\tau_h=\Delta t_h/\gamma=(1/2)(t_1-t_2)/\gamma$, exactly half the detector proper-time difference of step 4.1; explicitly $\Delta\tau_h=2\pi\Omega R^2/(c^2\sqrt{1-\Omega^2R^2/c^2})$. [L10, step 2.1, step 1.3, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 (Inertial limit and reversed rotation.) If $\Omega=0$ then $\gamma=1$, the meeting sets of step 2.2 are both $2\pi kR/c$, so $t_1=t_2=2\pi R/c$ and both differences of step 4.1 and both holonomies of step 5.1 vanish; the rest lines are the $t=\text{const}$ circles of step 1.3. If $\Omega<0$, the factor $4\pi\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$ of step 4.1 is negative, so the sign of $t_1-t_2$ is reversed, and the labels 'co-rotating' and 'counter-rotating' are interchanged because the material angular rate $\Omega$ now has the opposite sign to that of $C_+$. [L10, step 1.3, step 4.1, step 5.1, algebra]

The radar distance is not the rest distance: in the slice $\theta = \theta_m$ the two worldlines are at rest distance $|\rho_m - \rho_0|$, whereas for $\rho_m = 2\rho_0$ the radar distance is $\rho_0 \log 2 < \rho_0$, because $\log$ is strictly increasing and $e > 2$ implies $\log 2 < \log e = 1$ ([[cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]). For every distinct positive reflector radius the notions differ: with $r = \rho_m/\rho_0$, one has $\log r < r - 1$ when $r > 1$ and $-\log r > 1 - r$ when $0 < r < 1$. The two distance formulas agree only at $r = 1$, where both have the continuous degenerate value zero. The coincident case is not a nonzero emission-reflection-reception triple of the protocol, whose distinct-reflector hypothesis remains in force. As $\rho_m \to 0^+$ the round-trip proper time and the radar distance grow without bound while the reflector's proper acceleration $c^2/\rho_m$ diverges; as $\rho_m \to +\infty$ the round-trip proper time and the radar distance also grow without bound while the reflector's proper acceleration tends to $0$.

The boundary is $x^1=|x^0|$, split into the two half-planes $x^1=x^0\ge0$ (where $V=0$, $U\ge0$) and $x^1=-x^0\ge0$ (where $U=0$, $V\le0$); these are the parts of the full null planes $V=0$ and $U=0$ that bound $W$, while the full planes extend beyond. 1.2 (The worldline $O$ and its parametrization.) By [L3] the curve $\theta\mapsto\Phi(\theta,\rho_0,y_0,z_0)$ is a flow line of $n=\rho^{-1}\partial_\theta$ restricted to $\rho=\rho_0$; its tangent with respect to $\theta$ is $\partial_\theta=\rho_0 n$, so by [L4] its four-velocity is $cn$, its proper time satisfies $d\tau=\rho_0\,d\theta/c$, i.e. $\theta=c\tau/\rho_0$ up to an additive constant, and its proper acceleration is $c^2/\rho_0$. Since $w^2=w^3=0$, one has $\Delta U:=U(q)-U(p)=w^0+w^1$, $\Delta V:=V(q)-V(p)=w^0-w^1$, and $\Delta U\Delta V=(w^0)^2-(w^1)^2$; hence $w\in\bar C^+$ iff $\Delta U\ge0$, $\Delta V\ge0$ and $\Delta U\Delta V\ge0$, and $w$ is future null iff in addition $\Delta U\Delta V=(w^2)^2+(w^3)^2=0$, i.e. iff either $\Delta V=0<\Delta U$ or $\Delta U=0<\Delta V$. Differentiating $U=\rho e^{\theta}$ and $V=-\rho e^{-\theta}$ along a curve in $W$ gives $dU=e^{\theta}(d\rho+\rho\,d\theta)$ and $dV=-e^{-\theta}(d\rho-\rho\,d\theta)$, so the future null lines through a point of $O$ in the plane are exactly the constant-$U$ lines ($d\theta=-d\rho/\rho$) and the constant-$V$ lines ($d\theta=+d\rho/\rho$). [L3, L5, algebra]

2.1 (Causal criteria for the worldline $O$.) For an arbitrary displacement $w$, $w\in\bar C^+$ is equivalent to $\Delta U\ge0$, $\Delta V\ge0$ and $\Delta U\Delta V\ge(w^2)^2+(w^3)^2$: this follows from $w^0=(\Delta U+\Delta V)/2$ and $\eta(w,w)=-\Delta U\Delta V+(w^2)^2+(w^3)^2$ and the inertial cone criterion [L5]. (Forward.) Let $q\le p$ with $p$ on $O$, so $w=p-q\in\bar C^+$; then $\Delta V=V(p)-V(q)\ge0$ and $V(p)=-\rho_0e^{-\theta_p}<0$, so $V(q)\le V(p)<0$. Similarly $\Delta U\ge0$ with $U(p)>0$ gives nothing yet, but the same argument with the roles of $U$ and $V$ reversed and the sign of $\rho_0 e^{\theta_p}$ shows $U(q)\le U(p)$; to obtain $U(q)>0$ from $p\le q$ one uses $w=q-p\in\bar C^+$: then $U(q)-U(p)\ge0$ and $U(p)=\rho_0e^{\theta_p}>0$, so $U(q)\ge U(p)>0$; and $V(q)\ge V(p)$ gives no upper bound. (Reverse.) Suppose $V(q)<0$; choose $\theta_p$ with $-\rho_0e^{-\theta_p}>V(q)$, i.e. $V(p)>V(q)$, which is possible because $-\rho_0e^{-\theta_p}\to0^-$ as $\theta_p\to+\infty$; then $\Delta V>0$, and $\Delta U=\rho_0e^{\theta_p}-U(q)$ and $\Delta U\Delta V$ tend to $+\infty$ as $\theta_p\to+\infty$ while the transverse displacement $(y_0-q^2,z_0-q^3)$ is fixed, so for all sufficiently large $\theta_p$ the three general inequalities just established hold and $q\le p$. Similarly, if $U(q)>0$, choose $\theta_p$ very negative so that $U(p)=\rho_0e^{\theta_p}<U(q)$ and $\Delta U>0$, while $\Delta V=V(q)+\rho_0e^{-\theta_p}\to+\infty$; then $\Delta U\Delta V\to+\infty$ and $p\le q$ for all sufficiently negative $\theta_p$. The remaining consequences in (ii) follow by evaluating the signs of $U$ and $V$ on the horizon plane, the left wedge ($U<0<V$) and the future and past wedges. [L5, step 1.1, step 1.3, algebra]

4.1 (Clause (iii): the limiting cases.) As $\rho_m\to0^+$ we have $|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|\to+\infty$ by strict increase and unboundedness of $\log$ (equivalently $\log(\rho_0/\rho_m)\to+\infty$), so the round-trip proper time $(2\rho_0/c)|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ and the radar distance $\rho_0|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ grow without bound, while the reflector's proper acceleration $c^2/\rho_m\to+\infty$ by [L4]; as $\rho_m\to+\infty$ the same divergence of $|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ holds while $c^2/\rho_m\to0^+$. Explicitly, fix a future unit $n$ and a unit $e\in n^\perp$ and, for every integer $\gamma\ge2$, take the state with Lorentz factor $\gamma$, namely $|w|=c\sqrt{1-\gamma^{-2}}$ along $e$; [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) gives $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)$ while $\tfrac12m|w|^2=\tfrac12mc^2(1-\gamma^{-2})$, so $$T_n(P)-\tfrac12m|w|^2=mc^2\Bigl(\gamma-\tfrac32+\tfrac{1}{2\gamma^2}\Bigr)\to\infty\quad(\gamma\to\infty),$$ and the relative deviation from the Newtonian value equals $\frac{(2\gamma+1)(\gamma-1)}{\gamma+1}\to\infty$; the Archimedean property of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-of-archimedean]]) turns either display into the explicit violation of a prescribed $B$ at a sufficiently large integer $\gamma$. Consequently the constants $K(z_0)$ and $\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0$ of [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]] necessarily depend on the speed bound $z_0$, no bound of that form is uniform on the whole domain $|w|<c$, and $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma$ and $|q_n(P)|=mc\sqrt{\gamma^2-1}$ are unbounded as $|w|\to c$ although $\tfrac12m|w|^2\le\tfrac12mc^2$ there. The mechanism is explicit: the remainder is $R_E=mc^2R(z)$ with $|R(z)|\le K(z_0)z^2$, and $K(z_0)=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$ diverges as $z_0\uparrow1$ ([[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-expansion-of-observer-quantities]]).

An ideal massless particle of [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]] carries a nonzero future null four-momentum $P$ and, by [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)(i), satisfies $E_n(P)=c|q_n(P)|>0$ exactly; it has no four-velocity, proper time or relative velocity, and no rest mass, rest energy or kinetic energy is assigned to it. The hypotheses $m>0$ and $z\le z_0<1$ of [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]] exclude it, and no substitution $w$ with $|w|=c$ is available because $\gamma_w=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ is undefined there. The bridge therefore concerns massive particles only, and it neither derives nor constrains the ideal massless case or light.

3.1 (The four-dimensional extension.) Since $\tau$ is strictly increasing and $C^1$ with $\tau'=1/\gamma>0$, it has a $C^1$ inverse $t(\sigma)$ on $c\tau(J)$ with $dt/d\sigma=\gamma/c$ by [L6]; because $q$ is $C^2$, $\gamma$ is $C^1$ and $dt/d\sigma=(\gamma\circ t)/c$ is $C^1$, so $t$ is $C^2$. The image of $\Phi$ is the open set of events with $t\in J$, $x^1-q(t)\in I$, $x^2\in Y$ and $x^3\in Z$, with inverse $(\sigma,\xi,y,z)=(c\tau(t),x^1-q(t),x^2,x^3)$. The field $n=\gamma(1,\beta,0,0)$ has $\eta(n,n)=\gamma^2(-1+\beta^2)=-1$ and time component $\gamma>0$ with $|(n)_s|=\gamma|\beta|<\gamma$, so it is a future unit timelike field, $C^1$ because $q$ is $C^2$. 4.1 (Clause (b): the material-family analysis applies.) [F5] Exterior calculus: $d(\alpha\wedge\beta)=d\alpha\wedge\beta+(-1)^k\alpha\wedge d\beta$ for a $k$-form $\alpha$, $d^2=0$, $df=\sum_a\partial_af\,dx^a$ for functions in a chart, and $d\alpha_{ab}=\partial_a\alpha_b-\partial_b\alpha_a$ for one-forms ([[def-wedge-product-of-differential-forms]], [[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]], [[def-closed-and-exact-differential-forms]]).

[F6] Lie bracket: $[X,Y]^a=X^b\partial_bY^a-Y^b\partial_bX^a$ and $[fX,Y]=f[X,Y]-Y(f)X$ for a smooth function $f$ ([[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]]).

[F7] A tetra d at an event is an ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ and $e_0$ future; a congruence is a smooth field $n$ with $\eta(n,n)=-1$, $n$ future; a vector with components $(u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3)$ in an inertial frame is future timelike if and only if $-u^0{}^2+|\vec u|^2<0$ and $u^0>0$ ([[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]).

[F8] Chain rule and smoothness of composites of $C^1$ or smooth maps; the component function $\gamma(r)=(1-\Omega^2r^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ is smooth where $r<c/|\Omega|$ ([[thm-chain-rule]], [[def-derivative]]).
[F9] Flow box: a smooth nowhere-zero vector field on a smooth manifold is locally $\partial/\partial u^0$ in suitable coordinates ([[thm-flow-box-theorem]]).

1.1 Preservation (a): write $s$ for the given parameter and $\tau'(s)>0$ for its proper-time derivative. By [F1], $X'=\tau'c^{-2}(\eta(A,X)U-\eta(U,X)A)$ and likewise for $Y$. Bilinearity gives $\frac{d}{ds}\eta(X,Y)=\eta(X',Y)+\eta(X,Y')=\tau'c^{-2}[\eta(A,X)\eta(U,Y)-\eta(U,X)\eta(A,Y)+\eta(A,Y)\eta(U,X)-\eta(U,Y)\eta(A,X)]=0$. The two pairs cancel, so the scalar pairing is constant on the interval by [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]]; the fields are $C^1$, including continuity at any included endpoints. Norms and orthogonality are therefore preserved. For the unique transported fields with prescribed tetrad initial values, all pairings remain $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$, and the time leg is $U/c$ because [F1] makes $U/c$ transported with the same initial value. Hence the family remains an observer-adapted tetrad. [F1, F7, given]

1.2 Rindler coordinates (b), part 1: the map $\Phi(\theta,\rho,y,z)=(\rho\sinh\theta,\rho\cosh\theta,y,z)$ is smooth on $\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^2$ by [F4] and [F8], and its image is contained in $W$ because $\cosh\theta>|\sinh\theta|$ for every $\theta$; conversely, for $(x^0,x)$ with $x>|x^0|$ the numbers $\rho:=\sqrt{x^2-(x^0)^2}>0$ and $\theta:=\tfrac12\log\bigl((x+x^0)/(x-x^0)\bigr)\in\mathbb R$ are well defined and smooth, and the identities $\rho\sinh\theta=x^0$, $\rho\cosh\theta=x$ follow from $e^{\pm\theta}=\sqrt{(x\pm x^0)/(x\mp x^0)}$ and $\cosh^2-\sinh^2=1$; hence $\Phi$ is a bijection of its domain onto $W$ with smooth inverse. Differentiating the four component functions gives $dx^0=\sinh\theta\,d\rho+\rho\cosh\theta\,d\theta$ and $dx=\cosh\theta\,d\rho+\rho\sinh\theta\,d\theta$, so the pullback metric is $-(\sinh\theta\,d\rho+\rho\cosh\theta\,d\theta)^2+(\cosh\theta\,d\rho+\rho\sinh\theta\,d\theta)^2+dy^2+dz^2=d\rho^2-\rho^2d\theta^2+dy^2+dz^2$, the cross terms cancelling and the $\sinh^2-\cosh^2=-1$ identity producing the term $-\rho^2d\theta^2$. [F4, F8]

1.3 Rigid rotation (c), part 1: $K=\partial_0+(\Omega/c)(-x^2\partial_1+x^1\partial_2)$ is a smooth vector field on the whole chart, and $\eta(K,K)=-1+\Omega^2r^2/c^2<0$ exactly on the stated region $U_\Omega$ (and everywhere when $\Omega=0$) by [F2]; its components in the inertial chart are $K=(1,-\tfrac{\Omega}{c}x^2,\tfrac{\Omega}{c}x^1,0)$, so $K$ is future where it is timelike, and $\gamma(r)=(1-\Omega^2r^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ is smooth and positive on $U_\Omega$ by [F8], so $n=\gamma K$ satisfies $\eta(n,n)=\gamma^2(-1+\Omega^2r^2/c^2)=-1$ and is future unit, that is, a congruence on $U_\Omega$ with the stated observer field. Computing the symmetric derivative of the components $\eta_{ab}K^b=(-1,-\tfrac{\Omega}{c}x^2,\tfrac{\Omega}{c}x^1,0)$ gives $\partial_a(\eta K)_b+\partial_b(\eta K)_a=0$: the only nonzero first partials are $\partial_1(\eta K)_2=\Omega/c$ and $\partial_2(\eta K)_1=-\Omega/c$, which cancel in the symmetrization, so $K$ is a Killing field. [F2, F8]

1.4 Bell setup (d): for $q$ of class $C^2$ with $|q_1'|<c$, the functions $\gamma=(1-q_1'^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ and $\beta=q_1'/c$ are $C^1$ in $t$ by [F8], so the field $n(x)=\gamma\bigl(1,\beta,0,0\bigr)$ evaluated at $t=x^0/c$ is a $C^1$ future unit field on any open subset $\Omega$ of the chart with $\Omega\subseteq\{|q_1'(x^0/c)|<c\}$; it is tangent to the translated worldlines $x_\xi(t)=(ct,q(t)+\xi)$, since their coordinate derivative $(c,q_1',0,0)=c(1,\beta,0,0)$ is a positive multiple of $n$. The longitudinal unit vector $s=\gamma(\beta,1,0,0)$ satisfies $\eta(s,s)=\gamma^2(-\beta^2+1)=1$ and $\eta(n,s)=\gamma^2(-\beta+\beta)=0$, so $s$ is a unit rest vector of $n$. [F2, F7, F8]

e0$; by [F3] the vorticity $\omega$ is nowhere zero there and the ambient rest distribution is nowhere integrable, so no rest-simultaneity hypersurface exists locally. For $\Omega=0$ the field is $n=\partial_0$, which is inertial and irrotational with rest hypersurfaces $x^0=const$. [F2, F3, F5, step 1.3]

2.3 Bell deformation (d): with $\beta=q_1'/c$ and $\beta'=q_1''/c$, the components of $n$ are $n=(n^0,n^1,n^2,n^3)=(\gamma,\gamma\beta,0,0)$, hence $n_b=\eta_{bc}n^c=(-\gamma,\gamma\beta,0,0)$, and $n$ depends on the coordinates only through $t=x^0/c$, so $\partial_1n=\partial_2n=\partial_3n=0$ and $\partial_0=\tfrac1c\tfrac{d}{dt}$ by [F2]. Using $\tfrac{d\gamma}{dt}=\gamma^3\beta\beta'$ (from $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ and the chain rule) and $1+\gamma^2\beta^2=\gamma^2$ one gets $\partial_0n_0=-\gamma^3\beta\beta'/c$ and $\partial_0n_1=\tfrac1c\tfrac{d}{dt}(\gamma\beta)=\tfrac{\gamma^3\beta'/c}{1}$; contracting with $s=\gamma(\beta,1,0,0)$ gives $s^as^b\partial_an_b=(\gamma\beta)^2\bigl(-\gamma^3\beta\beta'/c\bigr)+(\gamma\beta)(\gamma)\bigl(\gamma^3\beta'/c\bigr)=\tfrac{\gamma^5\beta\beta'}{c}(1-\beta^2)=\tfrac{\gamma^3\beta\beta'}{c}=\gamma^3q_1'q_1''/c^3$, where $1-\beta^2=\gamma^{-2}$. Since $s$ is a rest vector ($\eta(n,s)=0$ by step 1.4), the projections act as the identity on $s$ and $\theta(s,s)=s^as^b\partial_an_b$ in the first-order sense; all transverse components of $\partial_an_b$ vanish because $n$ depends only on $t$, so $\theta(s,s)$ is nonzero exactly when $q_1'(t)q_1''(t)\ne0$, and then the first-order rigidity condition $\theta=0$ fails on a neighbourhood of $t$; the translated worldlines have, at every fixed chart time, the constant separation $|\xi_1-\xi_2|$, so this failure of Born rigidity is not in conflict with the constant labelling. No crack, fracture or elasticity conclusion is drawn. [F1, F2, F8, step 1.4]

3.1 Ring cylinder geometry (c), part 3: parameterize the cylinder $r=R$, $x^3=const$ by $(t,\varphi)$ with $x^0=ct$ and $\varphi=\phi-\Omega t$, so that the inertial angle is $\phi=\varphi+\Omega t$ and the point is $R(\cos\phi,\sin\phi)$. Substituting $d\phi=d\varphi+\Omega\,dt$ into $ds^2=-c^2dt^2+R^2d\phi^2$ gives the induced metric $-(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)dt^2+2\Omega R^2dtd\varphi+R^2d\varphi^2$, a nondegenerate Lorentzian metric on the cylinder since $|\Omega|R<c$. The observer with label $\phi_0$ has inertial angle $\phi(t)=\phi_0+\Omega t$, hence tangent $c\partial_0+\Omega R(-\sin\phi\,\partial_1+\cos\phi\,\partial_2)=cK$ evaluated at the ring, so its dimensionless four-velocity is $n=\gamma(R)K$ and its four-velocity is $cn$, whose components at the ring are $\gamma(R)(1,-(\Omega R/c)\sin\phi,(\Omega R/c)\cos\phi,0)$ as stated. The covector $\kappa$ of step 2.2 restricts to the cylinder as $\kappa=-c\,dt+(\Omega/c)R^2d\phi=-c\,dt+(\Omega R^2/c)(d\varphi+\Omega\,dt)=-\tfrac{c^2-\Omega^2R^2}{c}dt+\tfrac{\Omega R^2}{c}d\varphi$, so the ambient rest covector $n^\flat=\gamma(R)\kappa$ is proportional to $-(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)dt+\Omega R^2d\varphi$; its kernel on the cylinder is the line field generated by $\partial_\varphi+\tfrac{\Omega R^2}{c^2-\Omega^2R^2}\partial_t$, since the kernel condition is $-(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)dt(v)+\Omega R^2d\varphi(v)=0$ for $v=a\partial_t+b\partial_\varphi$, that is $-(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)a+\Omega R^2b=0$, so $v$ is a multiple of $\partial_\varphi+\tfrac{\Omega R^2}{c^2-\Omega^2R^2}\partial_t$; equivalently $dt/d\varphi=\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$ along rest lines. [F2, step 1.3, step 2.2]

4.1 Ring holonomy (c), part 4: the vector field $Z:=\partial_\varphi+	frac{\Omega R^2}{c^2-\Omega^2R^2}\partial_t$ on the cylinder is smooth and nowhere zero (the coefficient of $\partial_\varphi$ is $1$), so by the flow box theorem [F9] applied on the two-dimensional cylinder there are local coordinates in which $Z=\partial/\partial u^0$; in particular the rest line field is locally integrable, its integral curves satisfy $dt/d\varphi=	frac{\Omega R^2}{c^2-\Omega^2R^2}$ by the kernel computation of step 3.1, and integrating from $\varphi=0$ to $\varphi=2\pi$ at the initial label gives the signed offset $\Delta t=	frac{2\pi\Omega R^2}{c^2-\Omega^2R^2}$, which returns to the same rotating label $\varphi$ at a different chart time when $\Omega
e0$. If $f$ were a globally single-valued real function on the whole cylinder with $df=\mu\,(dt-	frac{\Omega R^2}{c^2-\Omega^2R^2}d\varphi)$ for a nowhere-zero time-oriented $\mu$ (so that the kernel of $df$ is exactly the rest-line distribution, so the level sets of $f$ are tangent to those lines), then the angular lift $F(\varphi):=f(0,\varphi)$ would have $F(0)=F(2\pi)$ by single-valuedness on the circle. Its derivative is $F'(\varphi)=-\mu(0,\varphi)\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$, with a fixed nonzero sign because the multiplier is time-oriented and $\Omega
e0$, $R>0$. The mean value theorem [[cor-mean-value-theorem]] on $[0,2\pi]$ therefore gives $F(2\pi)-F(0)=2\pi F'(\xi)
e0$ for some $\xi\in(0,2\pi)$; this contradiction shows that no such global synchronization function exists. The obstruction is the holonomy of the global ring and is distinct from the ambient pointwise nonintegrability of step 2.2, which is a local statement in the four-dimensional open set and does not apply to the one-dimensional rest line field on the cylinder. For $\Omega=0$ the kernel condition reads $dt=0$ and both the offset and the obstruction vanish. [F5, F9, step 3.1]

5.1 Conclusion: step 1.1 proves (a), including the preservation of norms and orthogonality and the observer-adapted tetrad; steps 1.2 and 2.1 prove (b), including the Rindler metric, the unit future field, the acceleration $\rho^{-1}\partial_\rho$, Born rigidity, vanishing vorticity, the rest slices and the non-coordinate-frame bracket; steps 1.3, 2.2, 3.1 and 4.1 prove (c), including the Born-rigid rotating congruence, its nowhere-zero vorticity and ambient nonintegrability for $\Omega\ne0$, the inertial case $\Omega=0$, the ring metric, the rest-line equation, the time offset $2\pi\Omega R^2/(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)$ and the impossibility of a globally single-valued ring synchronization time; and steps 1.4 and 2.3 prove (d), with the first-order deformation $\theta(s,s)=\gamma^3q_1'q_1''/c^3$ and the exclusion of material fracture claims. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 2.3] ∎

- **First-order versus smooth calculus.** Part (d) is deliberately stated for a $C^1$ field $n$ using the first-order clause of [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]]: only first derivatives of $n$ occur in the projected deformation, the result is a continuous tensor, and no smooth extension of the Bell congruence or its flow is asserted. When $q$ is smooth the formulas agree with the smooth congruence definitions of [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]].

- **Two different obstructions in part (c).** The ambient rest distribution over the four-dimensional rotating open set is nowhere integrable for $\Omega\ne0$ (nowhere-zero vorticity), while the one-dimensional rest line field on the ring cylinder is locally integrable with a nonzero global holonomy; the second is not an instance of the first, and no locally defined synchronization function on the cylinder can be single-valued around the ring.

regularity_scope_evidence: **(i) Flow box.** If $X$ is a smooth vector field on $\Omega$ ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]) and $X(p)\ne0$ at a point $p\in\Omega$, then there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $p$ in $\Omega$ and a chart $(u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3):U\to\mathbb R^4$ in which $X=\partial/\partial u^0$; the integral curves of $X$ in $U$ are therefore the $u^0$-coordinate lines up to reparametrization. In particular every observer congruence $n$ on $\Omega$ ([[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]]) admits a local $n$-adapted chart, and in such a chart $n=\partial/\partial u^0$.

**(ii) Frobenius criterion.** For a smooth nowhere-zero one-form $\alpha$ on $\Omega$ ([[def-closed-and-exact-differential-forms]]) let $D:=\ker\alpha$ be the hyperplane distribution $D_p=\{v\in V:\alpha_p(v)=0\}$. Then $D$ is integrable on $\Omega$ (through every point there passes a local hypersurface whose tangent space at each of its points is the corresponding $D_p$) if and only if $\alpha\wedge d\alpha=0$ on $\Omega$ ([[def-wedge-product-of-differential-forms]]).

**(iii) Rest distributions of observer congruences.** Let $n$ be an observer congruence on $\Omega$ ([[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]]), let $\alpha:=n^\flat$, and let $\theta,\omega$ be its expansion and vorticity ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]]). Then:

(a) $d\alpha=2
abla_{[a}n_{b]}$, that is, $d\alpha(X,Y)=(
abla_Xn^ lat)(Y)-(
abla_Yn^ lat)(X)$ for smooth vector fields $X,Y$;

(b) for every $p$ and all $X,Y$ with $\alpha(X)=\alpha(Y)=0$ one has $d\alpha(X,Y)=2\omega(X,Y)$; consequently $(\alpha\wedge d\alpha)(p)=0$ if and only if $\omega(p)=0$, and on an open set $U\subseteq\Omega$ the following are equivalent: $\alpha\wedge d\alpha=0$ on $U$, $\omega=0$ on $U$, and the rest distribution $\ker\alpha$ is integrable on $U$;

(c) when the rest distribution is integrable on $U$, its integral hypersurfaces are orthogonal to $n$ at every point and the restriction of $\eta$ to each of them is positive definite, so they are rest slices of the congruence.

**(iv) Scope.** All statements are local on $\Omega$; no global foliation, global synchronization, completeness or product structure is asserted, and no claim is made about variable-rank or non-smooth distributions.

**Given:** A nonempty open subset $\Omega$ of the affine Minkowski space $A$, the smooth structure of the inertial atlas, a smooth vector field $X$ on $\Omega$, a smooth nowhere-zero one-form $\alpha$ on $\Omega$, an observer congruence $n$ on $\Omega$ with $\alpha=n^\flat$, $n_b=\eta_{bc}n^c$, and its kinematic fields $\theta,\omega$ ([[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]], [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]], [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]]).

[F1] Flow box: if $X$ is a smooth vector field on a smooth manifold $M$ and $X_p\ne0$, then there are local coordinates $(u^1,\dots,u^n)$ near $p$ in which $X=\partial/\partial u^1$ ([[thm-flow-box-theorem]]).

[F2] Codimension-one Frobenius: for a nowhere-zero one-form $\alpha$ on a smooth manifold, the hyperplane distribution $\ker\alpha$ is integrable if and only if $\alpha\wedge d\alpha=0$ ([[cor-codimension-one-frobenius-criterion]], [[def-wedge-product-of-differential-forms]]).

[F3] The flat covariant derivative is torsion-free, $
abla_XY-
abla_YX=[X,Y]$, is metric compatible, acts on functions as the directional derivative and satisfies the product rule; in inertial components $
abla_a=\partial_a$ on components and $[X,Y]^a=X^b\partial_bY^a-Y^b\partial_bX^a$ ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]], [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], [[prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket]]).

[F4] For a smooth one-form $\alpha$ and smooth vector fields $X,Y$, $d\alpha(X,Y)=X(\alpha(Y))-Y(\alpha(X))-\alpha([X,Y])$, and $d\alpha$ is a smooth two-form with components $d\alpha_{ab}=\partial_a\alpha_b-\partial_b\alpha_a$ in any inertial chart ([[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]], [[def-closed-and-exact-differential-forms]]).

1.1 Flow box and adapted charts: the flat model with its inertial atlas is a smooth 4-manifold ([[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]]) and $X$ is a smooth vector field on the open set $\Omega$, so [F1] applied on this manifold gives coordinates $(u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3)$ on an open neighbourhood $U$ of $p$ with $X=\partial/\partial u^0$. In such a chart the coordinate representation of a curve $\gamma$ in $U$ satisfies $\gamma'=X\circ\gamma$ if and only if $(u^a\circ\gamma)'=\delta^a_0$ for every $a$, i.e. if and only if $u^1,u^2,u^3$ are constant and $u^0\circ\gamma$ is affine; hence the integral curves of $X$ in $U$ are exactly the $u^0$-coordinate lines, up to reparametrization. If $n$ is an observer congruence, then $n$ is nowhere zero by [F6], so applying the flow box to $X=n$ produces a chart with $n=\partial/\partial u^0$ in which $u^1,u^2,u^3$ are constant along every integral curve of $n$ contained in $U$; this is precisely an $n$-adapted chart in the sense of [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]] clause (d). reference_text: **(ii) Rotational case.** Let $U\subseteq\Omega$ be a flow box of $n$ with adapted coordinates $(s,y^1,y^2,y^3)$ in which $n=\partial_s$ ([[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]]), and suppose that $\omega$ is nowhere zero on $U$. Then the vorticity and the acceleration are **basic** on $U$: they are horizontal and their components in the adapted coframe do not depend on $s$, equivalently $\mathcal L_n\omega=0$ and $\mathcal L_na^\flat=0$. Moreover $da^\flat=0$ on $U$, and for every primitive $F$ of the closed one-form $a^\flat$ on the star-shaped box $U$ ([[thm-poincare-lemma-for-differential-forms-on-star-shaped-domains]]) the field $K:=e^Fn$ is a timelike Killing field, $\nabla_aK_b+\nabla_bK_a=0$, equivalently $\mathcal L_K\eta=0$. If $U$ is connected and simply connected and $\omega$ is nowhere zero, then a single positive smooth function $f$ on $U$ satisfies $\mathcal L_{fn}\eta=0$ ([[lem-sr-closed-one-form-primitive-on-simply-connected-open-sets]]). Conversely, every future timelike Killing field on a connected open set, normalized as $n=K/\sqrt{-\eta(K,K)}$, is Born rigid, and its vorticity is either nowhere zero or identically zero on that set; hence its flow is rotational, in the sense of case (ii), exactly when its vorticity is nowhere zero.

[F3] Flow box and adapted charts: a smooth nowhere-zero vector field is locally $\partial/\partial u^0$ in suitable coordinates, and every observer congruence admits local adapted charts; in particular $n=\partial_s$ in coordinates $(s,y^1,y^2,y^3)$ on a flow box $U$, and the integral curves of $n$ are its $s$-lines ([[thm-flow-box-theorem]], [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]], [[def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field]]).

[F13] Frobenius criterion for rest distributions: on an open set the rest distribution $\ker n^\flat$ is integrable if and only if $\omega=0$ there, if and only if $n^\flat\wedge d(n^\flat)=0$; when it is integrable, its integral hypersurfaces are the pointwise rest slices $n^\perp$ ([[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]], clause (iii)).

**(ii) Rotational case.** Let $U\subseteq\Omega$ be a flow box of $n$ with adapted coordinates $(s,y^1,y^2,y^3)$ in which $n=\partial_s$ ([[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]]), and suppose that $\omega$ is nowhere zero on $U$. If $U$ is connected and simply connected and $\omega$ is nowhere zero, then a single positive smooth function $f$ on $U$ satisfies $\mathcal L_{fn}\eta=0$ ([[lem-sr-closed-one-form-primitive-on-simply-connected-open-sets]]). Then on a sufficiently small neighbourhood $U$ of every point the connected leaves of the rest distribution are open subsets of affine hyperplanes: there are a smooth future timelike curve $z:J\to A$ with $\eta(z',z')=-1$ and a smooth function $\sigma:U\to J$ such that, with

the tubular label has derivative $1+\eta(z''\circ\sigma,x-z\circ\sigma)$, which is nonzero and is taken positive on $U$. reference_text: Let $x$ be an inertial chart of the affine Minkowski model with coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, let $B:=\prod_{a=0}^{3}[c_a,d_a]$ with $c_a<d_a$ be a closed axis-parallel box, and let $T$ be a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field on an open neighbourhood of $B$; put $f^b:=\partial_aT^{ab}$ (continuous on $B$) as in [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]. (a) (Box identity.) For each $b$, with $F_a^+:=\{x\in B:x^a=d_a\}$, $F_a^-:=\{x\in B:x^a=c_a\}$ and each face integral the Riemann integral over the remaining three coordinates, $$\int_B f^b\,d^4x=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\Big(\int_{F_a^+}T^{ab}\,d^3x-\int_{F_a^-}T^{ab}\,d^3x\Big).$$ (b) (Slice balance.) Write $K:=\prod_{i=1}^{3}[c_i,d_i]$ and, for $s\in[c_0,d_0]$, $Q^b(s):=\int_K T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$; this is finite and continuous in $s$. For $c_0\le s_1<s_2\le d_0$, $$Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)=\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K} f^b\,d^4x-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\Big(\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^+}T^{ib}\,d^3x-\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^-}T^{ib}\,d^3x\Big),$$ where $K_i^\pm$ are the two faces $x^i=d_i$, $x^i=c_i$ of $K$. (c) (Finite-flux conservation.) If $f=0$ on $[s_1,s_2]\times K$ and $T^{ib}=0$ on the side faces $[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^\pm$ for $i=1,2,3$, then $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$ for every $b$. The theorem concerns finite axis-parallel boxes in one inertial chart and is proved by the fundamental theorem of calculus. It does not assert a flux identity for arbitrary regions or hypersurfaces, does not assert that $Q^b$ transforms as a four-vector under a change of inertial chart, and asserts no conservation without the stated side-flux hypothesis; no noncompact or limiting statement is made. No choice principle is used.

For $c_0\le s_1<s_2\le d_0$, $$Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)=\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K} f^b\,d^4x-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\Big(\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^+}T^{ib}\,d^3x-\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^-}T^{ib}\,d^3x\Big),$$ where $K_i^\pm$ are the two faces $x^i=d_i$, $x^i=c_i$ of $K$. **Given:** The affine Minkowski model with an inertial chart $x$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), a closed nondegenerate axis-parallel box $B=\prod_{a=0}^3[c_a,d_a]$, and a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field $T$ on an open neighbourhood $U\supseteq B$ ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]); the components $T^{ab}$ are $C^1$ functions on $U$ and $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ with $\partial_a$ the coordinate partial derivatives. For a face $F_a^\pm$ of a box, its face integral is the Riemann integral of the restricted continuous function over the product of the remaining three coordinate intervals.
[F4] Every continuous function on a closed nondegenerate rectangle is Riemann integrable. ([[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]], [[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]])

[F5] If $n\ge1$ and $f:Q\to\mathbb R$ is continuous on a nondegenerate box $Q=\prod_{j<n}[a_j,b_j]$, then for every permutation of the coordinates the corresponding repeated Riemann integral exists and equals $\int_Qf$. ([[cor-repeated-riemann-integrals-on-rectangles]])
[F6] A continuous real function on a nonempty compact metric space is bounded above and below and attains a maximum and a minimum. ([[thm-extreme-value-metric]])

1.1 Claim (a). Fix $b$ and $a$. For each fixed tuple $y$ of the remaining three coordinates, the function $t\mapsto T^{ab}(t,y)$ is $C^1$ on $[c_a,d_a]$ as a function on that interval, with derivative $\partial_aT^{ab}(t,y)$, which is continuous and hence integrable by [F4]; [F1] gives $\int_{c_a}^{d_a}\partial_aT^{ab}(t,y)\,dt=T^{ab}(d_a,y)-T^{ab}(c_a,y)$. The function $(t,y)\mapsto\partial_aT^{ab}(t,y)$ is continuous on the box $B$, so its repeated integral in this order exists and equals $\int_B\partial_aT^{ab}\,d^4x$ by [F5] and [F2]; substituting the pointwise identity above gives $\int_B\partial_aT^{ab}\,d^4x=\int_{F_a^+}T^{ab}\,d^3x-\int_{F_a^-}T^{ab}\,d^3x$. The integrands are continuous on the box $B$, hence integrable by [F4]; summing the identities over $a=0,1,2,3$ with the linearity part of [F3] yields the box identity (a). [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5]

1.2 Claim (b), finiteness and continuity of $Q^b$. For each $s\in[c_0,d_0]$ the function $x\mapsto T^{0b}(s,x)$ is continuous on the compact box $K$, hence bounded and integrable by [F4] and [F6], so $Q^b(s)$ is a finite real number. For $s,r\in[c_0,d_0]$ and each $x\in K$, [F1] applied to $t\mapsto T^{0b}(t,x)$ gives $T^{0b}(s,x)-T^{0b}(r,x)=\int_r^s\partial_0T^{0b}(t,x)\,dt$; integrating over $K$ with [F2] and [F5] gives $Q^b(s)-Q^b(r)=\int_K\int_r^s\partial_0T^{0b}(t,x)\,dt\,dx$. By [F6] the continuous $|\partial_0T^{0b}|$ is bounded on the compact box $B$ by some $M_1<\infty$, so the absolute-value estimate [F3] and the constant integral give $|Q^b(s)-Q^b(r)|\le M_1\operatorname{vol}(K)|s-r|$, and $Q^b$ is (Lipschitz) continuous on $[c_0,d_0]$. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6]

2.1 Claim (b), slice-balance identity. The sub-box $[s_1,s_2]\times K$ is a closed nondegenerate axis-parallel box contained in $B$, and $T$ is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of $B$, hence on a neighbourhood of the sub-box. Applying the box identity of step 1.1 to this sub-box, the two faces with $a=0$ give $\int_K T^{0b}(s_2,x)\,d^3x-\int_K T^{0b}(s_1,x)\,d^3x=Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)$, and for $i=1,2,3$ the faces $F_i^\pm$ are the side faces $[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^\pm$ with the displayed signs; with the sub-box's interior equal to $(s_1,s_2)\times\operatorname{int}K$, this is exactly the stated identity. [F3, step 1.1, given]

4.1 Claims (a), (b) and (c) are proved in steps 1.1, 1.2 and 2.1, and 3.1. The argument uses only the fundamental theorem of calculus, Fubini's theorem for continuous functions on boxes and the elementary integral estimates; it concerns one inertial chart and finite axis-parallel boxes, asserts nothing for arbitrary regions, hypersurfaces or noncompact slices, and asserts no conservation without the stated side-flux hypothesis. All choices are finite; no choice principle is used. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

This page supplies the flat-spacetime force and continuum layer of the framework. It defines the symmetric stress-energy field class, its inertial component and scaling conventions, its four-force density $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ and the exact conservation terminology, and it proves the pointwise observer decomposition of a symmetric field into energy density, momentum density and rest stress together with its uniqueness. The compact-support machinery (the fundamental lemma, integration by parts and differentiation under the integral sign) supplies the first variation of the adopted scalar-field action, its Euler–Lagrange equation and the Hilbert stress-energy tensor defined by compactly supported metric variations, including the full off-shell divergence identity. Dust and perfect-fluid models are analysed through exact conservation equivalences, and the finite-box balance theorem gives the flux form of conservation by the fundamental theorem of calculus, with explicit side-flux terms and the vanishing-side-flux corollary. The Hodge decomposition of an alternating two-form for an observer, its quadratic invariants and the optional electromagnetic identification are also supplied here for later use. On the physical side, the page adopts the scalar-field, dust and perfect-fluid models with their SI units and observer readings, the total-tensor isolation premise, and then proves conditional local conservation for the three models and integrated conservation of the slice four-momentum of an isolated system on finite boxes. Nothing here asserts gravity, electromagnetic coupling, a force law, an equation of state, energy conditions, an angular-momentum theorem, a four-vector transformation of slice integrals or any empirical fact.

Worked computations for the forces and continuum page. The examples compute the boosted components of a dust tensor and the exact factorization of its boosted energy coefficient, the static uniaxial stress balance in which the stress but not the energy density is constrained, the finite-box flux identity checked on an explicit field with opposite-face cancellations and explicit transverse-area factors, a family of exact constant-velocity dust solutions with transverse density profile and finite-box constancy of the slice integrals, the null plane-wave scalar field with its conserved Hilbert tensor and the zero/nonzero branch of the profile derivative, and the perfect-fluid components in the rest and boosted frames with the exact energy-density shift. The counterexamples show that a prescribed covariant symmetric tensor of the form $F\eta^{-1}$ need not be conserved, and that zero local divergence alone does not conserve a finite slice integral when the side flux does not vanish. Every item is a mathematical computation or witness; none asserts a measurement, a material model or empirical evidence.
